Findings first. You are Gemini acting as an external architecture/refactoring advisor for ADL issue #203. Do not approve publication, merge, or closeout. Provide decomposition and architecture advice only.

Return strict JSON only with keys: verdict, reason, proposed_slices, architecture_advice, must_fix_before_publication, notes. Use verdict one of: split_required, split_recommended, keep_single_pr. For proposed_slices, include name, purpose, paths, depends_on, validation, risk.

Current issue/worktree state: branch codex/203-authority-serving-adapters-preparation, HEAD f7d81e9b74e96ff586bce4bec225b1c433e10ad4, dirty working tree with uncommitted remediation. This is decomposition evidence against current working state, not a final exact-head publication review. git diff --check is clean.

Current LoC against origin/main including uncommitted work: 56 files changed, +5157 -477, net +4680. Code-only excluding docs/json/md/locks/logs: +2988 -477, net +2511. Non-code lifecycle/proof: +2169 -0.

Pre-PR review found P1 concerns: raw-store bypass risk via DistributedCertificateStore::open/activate/authorize/revoke, AuthorityLedger::new/apply/authorize_mutation, and FencingStore::create/open/commit; and a too-thin PublishedStoreAuthorityReceiptView exposing only lineage_id, operation_id, generation, result_sha256 instead of only published OwnerCommit/Fence results with lineage, action class, adapter version, published generation, canonical result digest, and receipt digest.

Current uncommitted remediation adds authority access token types for certificate/lease/fencing stores and extends the published view. Relevant path clusters: adl-runtime/src/distributed/certificates.rs, fencing.rs, lease.rs, authority_protocol.rs, authority_store_adapters.rs, authority_reconciliation.rs, migration.rs, recovery.rs, transport/core.rs, transport/governed/*, placement.rs, projection.rs, resource_weather.rs, snapshot_catalog.rs, capability_advertisement.rs, adl-runtime/tests/distributed_identity_lease_authority.rs, distributed_certificates.rs, distributed_fencing.rs, distributed_lease.rs, distributed_migration.rs, distributed_recovery.rs, distributed_runtime_transport.rs, distributed_transport.rs, and .csdlc issue/proof artifacts.

Assess whether this should remain a single PR or be split. If split, propose the smallest reviewable module decomposition and dependency order. Focus especially on architecture boundaries among sealed raw certificate/lease/fencing stores, governed authority-serving adapter facade, migration/recovery integration, transport/projection/peripheral runtime caller migration, and proof/lifecycle evidence. Identify must-fix architectural risks before any PR publication.
